title: Check the changes and have it edit (desktop)

steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
You'll ask Claude to edit the todo.txt you made in Desktop practice 1.

You'll learn three new things today:

  1. How to read "what will change" before it edits
  2. How to decline and ask again when you don't like it
  3. How to see the changes again in Changes afterwards
  • Time: 10–15 minutes
  • You need: the computer you used for Desktop practice 1 (todo.txt in the Practice folder on your desktop)

faq.a: You need to install the app and create todo.txt first. Please start with Desktop practice 1.

steps.title: Open the app and start in the practice folder
steps.html:
1. Open the Claude app and click the Code tab at the top left.
  2. Click + New at the top left to start a new conversation.
  3. Check that the buttons under the typing box show Local and the Practice folder. If not, click the folder button → Open folder… and choose the practice folder. (Once chosen, it appears in the list.)
  4. Also check that the permission mode button on the right says Manual.

check.q: Can you see Local · Practice · Manual?

steps.title: If the start screen looks different
steps.html:
• If you can't see the Code tab, check you're signed in with a paid account and the app is up to date.
  • Choosing a folder works like 'Choose the folder to work in' in Desktop practice 1.
  • Click the permission mode button and choose Manual.

steps.title: First, ask it to read the file
steps.html: Paste or type the sentence below into the box and press Enter (return on a Mac).

check.q: Did the contents of todo.txt appear?

steps.title: If it can't find the file
steps.html:
• Claude only sees files in the folder you chose. Check that the folder under the typing box is Practice.
  • If there's no todo.txt, create it first: "Create a file called todo.txt and write 3 example to-dos for today".

steps.title: Notice it didn't ask permission?
steps.html:
When it only reads a file, nothing changes. So Claude shows it without asking.

It only asks when it creates or edits a file. Now let's ask it to make an edit.

steps.title: Ask it to make an edit
steps.html: Ask it to change the second line. This time the permission card also shows exactly what will change.
steps.code: In todo.txt, change line 2 to "Set up a lunch meeting"
steps.alt: A permission card showing changes with red and green lines

check.q: Did a permission card with red and green lines appear, like the picture?

steps.title: If no permission card appears
steps.html:
• Claude may still be thinking. Wait a few seconds.
  • If Claude asks something back (e.g. which line), type your answer and press Enter.
  • If it already says it made the change, the mode isn't Manual. Switch it to Manual; it's fine to move on to checking the result.

steps.title: How to read "what will change"
steps.html:
It looks strange at first, but just look at the colors.

- Red lineText that will be removed
+ Green lineText that will be added
Uncolored lineText that stays the same
Allow buttonYes, make this change
Deny buttonNo, don't change it

If the red line shows the old line 2 and the green line shows Set up a lunch meeting, it's what you asked for. Click Allow.

The buttons may be labeled Allow, Accept, Deny, Reject and so on. The one that gives permission is usually blue.

check.noLabel: The red and green lines look wrong

steps.title: If the changes aren't what you asked for
steps.html:
That's exactly when to click Deny. Then type it again in the box, e.g. "Change only line 2 to 'Set up a lunch meeting'".

The to-dos in your file are examples Claude chose in practice 1, so it's fine if the words differ from the picture. Just check that line 2 changes.

steps.title: See the result with your own eyes
steps.html:
1. In the Practice folder on your desktop, double-click todo.txt. Notepad (TextEdit on a Mac) opens.
  2. Check that line 2 now says Set up a lunch meeting.
  3. Once you've checked, close Notepad. Leaving it open while Claude edits again can be confusing.
steps.alt: Checking in Notepad that line 2 changed

check.q: Does line 2 now say 'Set up a lunch meeting'?

steps.title: If you don't see the change
steps.html:
• If you opened Notepad before the edit, close it and open it again.
  • Ask Claude, "Show me what todo.txt says now."
  • If you clicked Deny, the file didn't change. Go back to the edit step and try again.

steps.title: Click "Deny" on purpose
steps.html:
Now let's practice what to do when you don't like something. Denying doesn't change the file at all, so don't worry.

  1. Send the sentence below.
  2. When the permission card shows the title Claude chose, click Deny.
steps.code: Add a title at the top of the to-do list
steps.alt: Clicking Deny and typing what you want instead

steps.title: If declining doesn't work
steps.html:
• There are two buttons under the permission card. Deny is the one that is not the permission button (usually blue).
  • If you clicked Allow by mistake, just say "Undo the change you just made."

steps.title: Say what you want instead
steps.html: After denying, just type what you want in the box.

check.q: Did you see '+ Today's to-dos' as a green line and click Allow?

steps.title: Look at the changes again — Changes
steps.html:
When a conversation gets long, it's easy to lose track of what changed. Then look at Changes (the list of changed files) on the right of the screen.

Click a line like todo.txt +2 -1 to see today's changed lines again in red and green.

Can't see Changes? Look for a panel button at the top right of the screen, or Changes in the menu.
steps.alt: Looking at the changes again under Changes on the right

check.q: Did you find the changed lines in Changes?

steps.title: If you can't find Changes
steps.html: Its place differs between app versions. Try the buttons at the far right or along the top of the screen. It's fine if you can't find it: today's key point is reading the permission card and choosing Allow or Deny.

steps.title: 🎉 Desktop practice 2 done! What you learned
steps.html:
You checked changes before they happened, and asked again when needed.

Three things to remember

  1. It doesn't ask when it reads a file; it only asks when it creates or edits one.
  2. On the permission card, red lines will be removed and green lines will be added.
  3. If you don't like it, Deny and say it again. The file stays as it was.

Why does this matter?

AI sometimes changes things differently from what you asked. As long as you have the habit of reading the changes before clicking Allow, your files won't change unexpectedly. It's the most important habit for using AI agents safely.

Next step

Next you'll learn how to start a new conversation and continue earlier ones. We'll post it as soon as it's ready.
